implementation.temperate_crownlet: one 9x18 distance-stable core plus three deterministic embedded 5x10 satellite volumes
implementation.conifer_change: six-to-eight azimuth-varied branches per tier, bounded storm-shortened branches, staggered branch heights, eleven overlapping asymmetric crown-body volumes, and an 8.5 m trunk ending at the highest whorl
implementation.broadleaf_change: the retained V2 branch family now uses compound four-volume crownlets instead of one ellipsoid per crown mass
implementation.collision: disabled presentation-only vegetation; river physics, bathymetry, solver fields, water authority, and raft forces unchanged

external_asset_audit.reason: Every available external or native-review tree family was either explicitly rejected at the fixed cameras or contract-limited to isolated comparison use.
not_promoted: Poly Haven Fir Tree 01: sparse pole silhouette in active river cameras
Poly Haven Tree Small 02: non-native structure analog and pale repeated crown
Poly Haven Futaleufu island and temperate forest sets: branch-card breakup and unstable distance crowns
Futaleufu cordilleran-cypress V1-V43: retained diagnostic research only; every production corridor substitution remains rejected
Poly Haven Pine Tree 01: rights-reviewed but still limited to isolated South Fork comparison, not automatic production replacement

accepted_findings: The conifer family retains a coherent tapered crown at guide-seat and river-eye distance instead of the repeated bare-pole/diamond-tip silhouette that dominated V2.
Broadleaf, shrub, ground-cover, and conifer forms all gain deterministic asymmetric crown edges without alpha cards or new external rights dependencies.
Both regenerated runnable maps preserve 6200 total vegetation instances, the 4650/1550 canopy-understory split, live solver water, player raft, game mode, and focused runtime-map contracts.
Two early V3 brackets that exposed spear trunks were rejected and not retained; the final trunk stops at the highest whorl and the conifer crown includes an overlapping distance-stable body.
remaining_photoreal_blockers: The project-owned tree family still has only one broadleaf and one conifer morphology; individual crown volumes remain visibly procedural at close range.
Exact Patagonian and Chilcotin species identity, ecology, seasonal state, wind response, guide review, and measured desktop/VR performance remain external acceptance gates.
The retained fixed views still show broad simplified bank surfaces, sparse near-bank micro-vegetation, and water that is too flat, dark, and uniform for photoreal approval.
A production canopy still needs multiple dense distance-stable rights-reviewed adult tree variants or a more detailed first-party botanical pipeline with production LODs.
